    Description
    io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Fact.setName(String)
    Create a new fact with new Fact<>(name, value), or set a value by name with FactStore.setValue(String, Object). Facts are expected to become immutable in 2.0.
    io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Fact.setValue(T)
    Create a new fact with new Fact<>(name, value), or set a value by name with FactStore.setValue(String, Object). Facts are expected to become immutable in 2.0.

    io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.FactReference.setValue(T)

    io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Rule()
    Use Rule.builder(). A binder can build rules through Rule.RuleBuilder instead; see the class description. Rule is expected to become immutable in 2.0, without this constructor.
    io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Rule(String, String, String, Integer, String)
    Use Rule.builder() instead. A positional constructor's parameters change whenever a field is added, and this constructor is expected to be removed in 2.0.
    io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Rule(String, String, String, Integer, String, String)
    Use Rule.builder() instead. A positional constructor's parameters change whenever a field is added, and this constructor is expected to be removed in 2.0.
    io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Rule.canEqual(Object)
    Rule is expected to become a final class in 2.0, so it can't be subclassed and doesn't need this method.
    io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Rule.setAction(String)
    Build the rule with Rule.builder(), or copy it with a change with Rule.toBuilder(). Rule is expected to become immutable in 2.0, without setters.

    io.github.brantunger.unruly.core.AbstractRulesEngine.JIT_PROPERTY
    The engine no longer changes MVEL's optimizer, so this property is ignored.
    io.github.brantunger.unruly.core.StatefulRulesEngine(Supplier<O>)
    Create the engine with RulesEngineBuilder.stateful(Supplier) instead. The engine classes are implementation details and are expected to become package-private in 2.0.

    Create the engine with RulesEngineBuilder.stateful(Supplier, int) instead. The engine classes are implementation details and are expected to become package-private in 2.0.
